title: "Breakout room - Is Bioconductor FAIR?"

## Scenario

The Bioconductor **FAIR data sharing** working group:

- [Bioconductor Working Groups: Guidelines and activities](https://workinggroups.bioconductor.org/currently-active-working-groups-committees.html#fair-data-sharing) provides a brief description of the working group

- [#fair-data-sharing](https://community-bioc.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/609880-fair-data-sharing) is the dedicated communication channel on the Bioconductor Zulip Chat <https://chat.bioconductor.org/>

Key outputs to date:

- [savingBiocObjects](https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/workflows/html/savingBiocObjects.html) workflow package
  + Vignette [Saving Bioconductor Objects for Sharing](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows/vignettes/savingBiocObjects/inst/doc/savingBiocObjects.html)

## Activity

The Bioconductor community has long emphasised interoperability between packages across its ecosystem, as well as support for standard bioinformatics file formats.

With the rapid development of new analytical methods, increasingly assisted by AI, ensuring that rich biological datasets can be shared and reused effectively is more important than ever.

The Bioconductor FAIR data sharing working group was established to develop recommendations, documentation, and training materials for users, particularly those new to Bioconductor. It also provides a forum to explore future directions for software development, both within Bioconductor and across other open-source communities, to support the sharing and reuse of rich datasets.

### User experience

Consider the first vignette, [Saving Bioconductor Objects for Sharing](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows/vignettes/savingBiocObjects/inst/doc/savingBiocObjects.html), from the [savingBiocObjects](https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/workflows/html/savingBiocObjects.html) workflow package.

- **Accessibility:** How approachable is this vignette for someone new to R or Bioconductor?

- **Prerequisites:** What knowledge or skills might beginners need before working through it?

- **Signposting:** What additional resources, documentation, or tools should the vignette point users towards?

- **Learning path:** Where does this vignette fit in a user's learning journey, and what should they already know or be able to do before engaging with it?
